newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cosipa gets 385 mln real BNDES loan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cosipa gets 385 mln real BNDES loan.

text.p: Brazilian private steelmaker Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) has signed a loan agreement with Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) for 385 million reais ($356.5 million).
BNDES President Carlos Mendonca de Barros said the loan will help finance Cosipa's 691 million real ($639.8 million) investment program to modernize the company and regain its competitive edge.

The funds will go to modernizing technology, improving product quality, reducing costs, increasing productivity and reducing the environmental impact of Cosipa's steel mill in Cubatao, Sao Paulo state.
Cosipa President Marcos Tambasco said most of the BNDES loan would be used to modernize the company's technology, which would help Cosipa post a net profit in 1998.

The steelmaker posted a net loss for 1996 of 249 million reais ($230.6 million) partly due to an increase in financial costs to pay for ongoing investments since its privatization in August 1993. First quarter results this year also showed a net loss of 28.4 million reais ($26.3 million). ((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
